【原视频简介】
Traditional RC helicopters rely on complex swashplates with lots of linkages, bearings, and moving parts. It makes you wonder: why make it so complicated? Why not just mount the entire main motor on a 2-axis pivot and use two high-torque servos to tilt the thrust vector directly? 

In this video, I built a custom 3D-printed test helicopter powered by an ESP32-S3 to test this exact concept. On the bench, the mechanism moves cleanly—but once the rotor spins up to speed, gyroscopic forces take over. Here is the complete build breakdown, the field flight test, and the physics behind why this setup flips over.

📥 3D Models (STL Files) & ESP32-S3 Source Code:

--------------------------------------------------
🔗 Referenced Videos & Demonstrations:
• Veritasium Gyroscopic Precession Demonstration: https://youtu.be/ty9QSiVC2g0?si=4qKFhZFxenYbmR3r
• Working Single-Motor Drone (Airflow Control Fins): https://youtu.be/BYTEedF-RXE?si=hCvCHixJEA5HK7BY

--------------------------------------------------
🛠️ Build Hardware & Specifications:
• Flight Controller: Custom ESP32-S3 Board
• Motion Sensor (IMU): MPU-9250
• Tilting Servos: 2x TowerPro MG996R All-Metal Gear (180°, 11 kg·cm stall torque @ 6V)
• Receiver Protocol: TBS Crossfire (CRSF)
• Power System: 3S LiPo Battery
• Voltage Regulator: 5A Step-Down Buck Converter (12V to 6V)
• Tail System: Direct-drive brushless motor & ESC for yaw
